subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Financial Literacy Limits
description: Learn Financial Literacy Limits in one minute.

hook.text: A study trained workers on compound interest, budgeting, and risk. Six months later, their saving behavior.

buildup.text: Financial literacy programs assume knowledge drives behavior. But research shows the link between financial knowledge.

discovery.text: Fernandes found financial education explains only 0.1% of variance in financial behavior.

twist.text: Just-in-time education works better: teach budgeting when taking a mortgage, not years before.

climax.text: Education matters but is insufficient alone. Combine it with nudges and structural changes for actual behavior change.

punchline.text: Knowing what to do and doing it are different problems.

quiz.question: Why is financial literacy education alone insufficient?
options: Financial content is too complex to teach
Knowledge explains very little of the variance in actual financial behavior
People forget everything within a day

details.summary: Financial literacy programs aim to improve economic decisions through education, but evidence shows they have modest and short-lived effects. People forget what they learn quickly, and knowledge alone does not overcome the behavioral biases that drive poor financial choices.
details.whyItMatters: Billions are spent on financial literacy programs with limited evidence of lasting impact. Recognizing these limits redirects policy toward nudges, defaults, and product regulation that work with human nature rather than trying to educate it away.
takeaways: Financial literacy programs show modest effects that decay rapidly
Knowledge alone does not overcome present bias and other behavioral barriers
Structural interventions like defaults are more effective than education alone

faq.question: Why don't financial literacy programs work as well as expected?
faq.answer: People forget information quickly, especially when it is not immediately relevant. And even when people know the right answer, behavioral biases like present bias, overconfidence, and inertia prevent them from acting on that knowledge.

faq.question: Should we abandon financial literacy programs entirely?
faq.answer: No, but they should be redesigned. Just-in-time education delivered at the moment of decision is more effective than classroom training. Combining education with structural supports like auto-enrollment and simplified products multiplies the impact.
